name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's ~23-point Republican partisan lean in the Texas Panhandle
Jackson's massive financial edge: $5.4M on hand vs. Nair's $14K
Polymarket prices the Democrat at only about 4%
No public polling or expert ratings treat this as competitive
model.rationale: The 13th District's 23-point Republican lean, Ronny Jackson's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the Democrat near 4% all point to a comfortable incumbent win, with no competitive signals in polls or ratings to suggest otherwise.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal involving Jackson or an unusually large national Democratic wave is the only realistic path to this race tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 13th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Ronny Jackson, the incumbent, is seeking another term and holds an enormous financial edge: he has raised about $4 million and reports more than $5.4 million on hand, while Democrat Mark Nair has raised roughly $100,000 with about $14,000 in the bank. Outside spending has supported Jackson with nothing opposing him.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters list it as contested. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 4 percent chance of an upset. The forecast expects Jackson to win comfortably, with the district's partisan makeup and the fundraising gap doing most of the work; only an extraordinary shift in the national environment would put the outcome in doubt.
